label: 9th original token (t=8), plus j/r at t=7; token-modulated
explanation: A late-position detector that fires only in the original phase. 90% of activation mass is at t=8, the 9th original token, which only exists when L=9 and is always the last token before <DEL>. On its own, t==8 gives dev F1 0.72 and mass recall 0.90, and 64% of t=8 steps are active. The remaining ~10% of mass is at t=7. Which token is input modulates both firing and magnitude: j and r fire on almost every t=8 step (precision 0.998) and are the strongest (top activations are j/r at t=8), and j/r also fire at t=7 (precision 0.61). The tokens e, u, t, z, g, w and 0 at t=8 are often inactive. It never fires at t<=5, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, and it essentially never fires in sequences with L<=7. The token dependence beyond j/r is graded and not fully captured, so precision stays incomplete.
